articles.title: Fifth Wall’s Brendan Wallace On Spotting Real Estate’s Next Hot Tech Early
articles.narrative: This article profiles Brendan Wallace, founder of Fifth Wall, a prominent investment firm focused on real estate technology. Wallace discusses his lifelong connection to real estate, influenced by his father's experiences as a New York City landowner, including a notable eminent domain case involving the site of the New York Times Building. He emphasizes his belief in land as a scarce, anti-inflationary asset that consistently appreciates in value. Wallace also reflects on his career path, from working in real estate groups at Goldman Sachs and Blackstone, where he learned from Jon Gray during major transactions like the Equity Office Properties Trust and Hilton Hotels buyouts, to ultimately founding Fifth Wall to invest in technology for the built environment.

data_points.address: 41st Street and Eighth Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Site was subject to an eminent domain dispute in the early 2000s.
data_points.project_notes: The Wallace family had owned the lot since 1886. The State of New York acquired the land for $12 million, though the family valued it at $30 million.

articles.title: Power Tech & AI 2026
articles.narrative: This article highlights the pervasive influence of artificial intelligence (AI) across various facets of commercial real estate (CRE), from data analysis and building operations to leasing, sales, and lending. AI is identified as the primary driver behind the robust data center market and is being integrated into established software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms. While the industry is currently in a "honeymoon period" with AI, experts anticipate an accelerated pace of adoption, particularly within institutional real estate. However, the number of standalone AI firms serving CRE is expected to consolidate due to competition and the efficiencies brought about by AI itself.

articles.title: Teresa Stephenson of Platinum Forbes Global Properties: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: This article features an interview with Teresa Stephenson, president of Platinum Forbes Global Properties, discussing her career transition from acting to real estate and her leadership philosophy. Stephenson emphasizes the firm's commitment to a boutique brokerage model, focusing on agent support and client service amidst industry consolidation. She highlights the importance of global reach for agents and the firm's high staff-to-agent ratio as key differentiators.

articles.title: Miami-Dade Office Rents Rise and Vacancy Tightens
articles.narrative: Miami-Dade County's office market continues to demonstrate strength with declining vacancy rates and increasing asking rents, according to a new report from Savills. The market's activity is notably bifurcated, with significant leasing in both the affordable Airport West submarket and the high-end Brickell financial district. While overall leasing activity has slowed, the scarcity of large office spaces in the county presents a potential challenge for future economic growth and attracting major corporate presences.

articles.title: Gravity Fitness Signs 23K-SF Lease at Queens’ Flushing Plaza
articles.narrative: Gravity Fitness has signed a long-term lease for 23,000 square feet at Flushing Plaza in Queens, New York. The athletic club will occupy the ground floor of the two-story office and retail complex, with plans to open in mid-2027. This lease underscores the demand for health and wellness options in the thriving Downtown Flushing community, which features a diverse mix of commercial and retail offerings.
tenants: Charles P. Wang Health and Wellness Center

articles.title: Subtext Completes Two Student Housing Developments in Florida, Tennessee
articles.narrative: Subtext has completed two student housing developments: VERVE Orlando, a 626-bed community near the University of Central Florida, and EVER Knoxville, a 498-bed property near the University of Tennessee. Both projects offer a wide array of amenities designed for student living, including fitness centers, study lounges, and various recreational spaces. VERVE Orlando was developed in partnership with FrontRange Capital Partners and Nuveen Real Estate, while EVER Knoxville was a collaboration with FrontRange Capital and TPG Real Estate Partners.

articles.title: Walmart to Open 40,344 SF Grocery Store in Metro Miami
articles.narrative: Walmart has signed a 40,344-square-foot retail lease at Doral Atrium, a 78,000-square-foot lifestyle retail development in Doral, Florida. The retailer plans to open a new neighborhood-format grocery store, with construction slated to begin this fall and an opening anticipated in 2027. The project is attracting a strong tenant mix, indicating robust retail demand in the area.

data_points.notable_features: Part of a 78,000-square-foot lifestyle retail development.
data_points.project_notes: Construction of the new store is expected to begin in Fall 2026.

articles.title: Pappas Properties Breaks Ground on Publix-Anchored Retail Center in Metro Charlotte
articles.narrative: Pappas Properties has commenced construction on a new Publix-anchored retail center within the 84-acre Cadia Village Matthews mixed-use development in metro Charlotte. The approximately 50,000-square-foot grocery store, which will include a drive-thru pharmacy, is slated for a fourth-quarter 2027 opening. The broader retail village will also feature medical offices, a bank, various dining options, and neighborhood services, complementing the residential component being developed by David Weekley Homes.

data_points.notable_features: Publix-anchored retail center with a drive-thru pharmacy, part of an 84-acre mixed-use campus.
data_points.project_notes: The mixed-use project also includes single-family homes and townhomes.

articles.title: JLL Arranges $53M Refinancing for Apartment Community in Huntsville
articles.narrative: JLL has arranged a $53 million refinancing loan for Arcadia Huntsville, a 250-unit apartment community in Huntsville, AL. The property, developed by Bobo Development Group and completed in 2024, is located within the Cumming Research Park. Revitate is a limited partner in the project.

data_points.notable_features: Features 18,000 square feet of retail, a heated saltwater pool, clubhouse with demonstration kitchen, fitness center, coworking space, dog park, electric vehicle charging stations, and outdoor grilling stations and lounge areas with gas fire pits.

articles.title: KBS Sells 297,591 SF Tollway North Office Park in Plano
articles.narrative: KBS has sold the 297,591-square-foot Tollway North Office Park in Plano, Texas, to BH Properties. The seven-building campus, situated on approximately 27 acres within Legacy Business Park, was approximately 70 percent leased at the time of sale. The property is designed to accommodate a diverse tenant base, including life sciences, light industrial, and traditional office users.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-building campus within Legacy Business Park, capable of supporting life sciences and light industrial users.

articles.title: Colliers closes sale of Mohr Logistics Park Building 6 in Whiteland
articles.narrative: Colliers has successfully brokered the sale of Mohr Logistics Park Building 6, a substantial 1,057,350-square-foot industrial facility in Whiteland, Indiana. The property, fully leased to a global power technology company through August 2036, was sold by Mohr Capital, which also developed the facility. This transaction highlights the continued demand for large-scale, well-located industrial assets in the Indianapolis market, particularly those offering strategic access to major transportation hubs and corporate supply chains.

data_points.notable_features: Features 40-foot clear height, 120 dock doors, four drive-in doors, 652 auto parking spaces, 270 trailer parking spaces, and a 140-foot truck court. Provides convenient access to Indianapolis International Airport and a global power technology company's corporate and supply-chain presence.
data_points.project_notes: Developed as Building 6 within the 475-acre Mohr Logistics Park, a master-planned industrial development projected to total over 6 million square feet at full buildout.

articles.title: Partners Land Fund I brokers sale of 16.7-acre land parcel at Waco Gateway Park
articles.narrative: Partners Land Fund I, an investment vehicle of Partners Capital, has sold a 16.7-acre industrial parcel within Waco Gateway Park to Partners Development Company, the development arm of Partners Real Estate. This transaction, which closed in August, marks the first significant industrial sale from the 153-acre park, originally acquired by the fund in November 2023. Proceeds from the sale will be used to finance infrastructure development within the park, including the extension of Gateway Boulevard and the installation of municipal utilities.

data_points.notable_features: The parcel is part of a 153-acre site zoned for light industrial use, with direct access to Interstate 35.
data_points.project_notes: The 153-acre Waco Gateway Park was initially acquired by Partners Land Fund I in November 2023. Proceeds from this sale will fund infrastructure development, including the extension of Gateway Boulevard and municipal utilities.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap brokers sale of three-property retail portfolio in West Allis
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of the Southtown Shopping Center, a three-property retail portfolio in West Allis, Wisconsin. The portfolio, which includes a Panera Bread outlot and a Krispy Kreme ground lease, was 98% leased at the time of sale with a strong weighted tenant tenure of nearly 16 years. The buyer, an East Coast-based 1031-exchange investor, was procured by Marcus & Millichap.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio includes a Panera Bread outlot and a Krispy Kreme ground lease; features a 15.88-year weighted tenant tenure.

articles.title: Charter Construction celebrates topping-out of The Motley in Midtown Nashville
articles.narrative: Charter Construction has celebrated the topping out of The Motley's first residential tower, a 26-story building located at 1401 Church St. in Midtown Nashville. This milestone marks the completion of the concrete structure for the tower, which will feature 326 rental residences and ground-floor retail. The project is being developed by IPB Properties and is part of a larger three-tower community planned to include nearly 1,200 residences and various commercial uses.

data_points.notable_features: Includes ground-floor retail and extensive resident amenities; design incorporates architectural references to the property's previous industrial use.
data_points.project_notes: Developed on the former Country Delite Farms property.

articles.title: Publix to Anchor Retail Component of Matthews Planned Development
articles.narrative: Pappas Properties has commenced the retail phase of its 82-acre Cadia Matthews mixed-use development, with sitework nearing completion and vertical construction anticipated to begin in late fall. The retail component, anchored by a grocery chain, will feature a 120,000-square-foot commercial village, including a bank and a 12,000-square-foot medical office building. The initial retail buildings are slated for delivery in June, followed by a quick-service restaurant next fall. The broader master-planned development will ultimately encompass 570 residential units, comprising both for-sale and rental properties.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use development with retail, medical office, and residential components.
data_points.project_notes: The development will include a mix of for-sale and rental residential units. First retail buildings scheduled for delivery in June, quick-service restaurant next fall.

articles.title: CREFC Sentiment Index Reaches Lowest Level in Three Years
articles.narrative: The CRE Finance Council's (CREFC) Third-Quarter 2026 Board of Governors Sentiment Index has dropped to its lowest point in three years, falling 17.5% to 83.3. This broad-based decline reflects significant concerns among members regarding the negative impact of mortgage and capitalization rates on commercial real estate finance businesses, with 92% of respondents anticipating adverse effects. The sentiment also indicates a growing pessimism about the U.S. economy's performance over the next 12 months, with 62% expecting a worsening outlook, driven by worries extending beyond immediate Federal Reserve decisions to broader issues like inflation, fiscal deficits, and long-term borrowing costs.

articles.title: INDUS Starts Work on 500K-SF Nashville-Area Warehouse Facility
articles.narrative: INDUS Realty Trust has secured $36.1 million in construction financing for the initial phase of INDUS Commerce Center @ 840, a speculative logistics facility spanning 507,000 square feet in Lebanon, TN. The project, located approximately 30 miles east of downtown Nashville, is designed to eventually expand into a 2.2 million-square-foot master-planned industrial park. Construction is set to commence immediately.

data_points.notable_features: Located directly off Interstate 840 in Wilson County, with close access to interstates 40, 24 and 65, and near Smyrna Airport and Nashville International Airport.
data_points.project_notes: The five-year, floating-rate loan is for the first phase of a master-planned park intended to include two to three additional buildings ranging from 400,000 to 1 million square feet.

articles.title: Woodfield Acquires West Palm Beach Condos at Auction
articles.narrative: Woodfield Development acquired an 84-unit, 13-building condominium community in West Palm Beach, FL, for $13.5 million through an auction. The property, located at 2800 Georgia Avenue, includes a 0.32-acre clubhouse and pool parcel. The sale was notable as the development had accumulated over $1.5 million in unpaid water bills, and the site offers significant redevelopment potential with existing MF-20 zoning and potential for increased density under affordable housing overlays.

data_points.address: 2800 Georgia Avenue, West Palm Beach, FL
data_points.notable_features: Existing MF-20 zoning permits up to 20 dwelling units per acre, with potential for up to 40 dwelling units per acre under the city's Affordable and Workforce Housing Overlay.
data_points.project_notes: The development was over $1.5 million behind in paying its water bills.

articles.title: BKM Pays $103M for Orlando Industrial Portfolio
articles.narrative: BKM Capital Partners and Kayne Anderson Real Estate have acquired a four-property, 543,000-square-foot light industrial portfolio in Central Orlando for $103 million. This acquisition expands BKM's Central Florida industrial holdings to over one million square feet across 13 properties. The portfolio, which is 95% occupied, will undergo a significant capital improvement plan to revitalize the assets.

data_points.notable_features: The portfolio comprises seven buildings and 22 units, offering clear heights of 16 to 28 feet and a 1:4,000-square-foot loading ratio.
data_points.project_notes: Two properties will join BKM's Gridline Orlando portfolio, while the other two will operate as standalone assets. The portfolio has a 4.3-year weighted average lease term (WALT).

articles.title: Multifamily's Days As Commercial Real Estate's 'Golden Child' Are Over
articles.narrative: The multifamily real estate sector is facing significant headwinds due to elevated borrowing costs and an oversupply of units, leading to a shift in investor focus. This challenging environment suggests that multifamily's era as the "golden child" of commercial real estate has concluded.

articles.title: Hedge Fund Breaks NYC Record With $375-Per-SF Office Lease
articles.narrative: Castle Hook Partners has secured a record-setting office lease at Related Cos.' upcoming 625 Madison Ave. The hedge fund's deal, valued at $375 per square foot, marks the highest price ever paid for office space in New York City.

data_points.address: 625 Madison Ave, New York City, NY

articles.title: Renewals Dominate In Years-Low Office Leasing Quarter
articles.narrative: The office leasing market experienced its lowest quarterly activity in years, primarily driven by lease renewals rather than new deals. This trend is attributed to escalating build-out costs and a scarcity of new office developments, prompting companies to opt for extending their current leases.

articles.title: Healey Nominates New Opportunity Zones, Targeting Sites Of Major Projects
articles.narrative: The Healey administration has released its proposed map for new Opportunity Zones, identifying areas with significant development potential. This initiative aims to stimulate economic growth and investment in designated low-income communities by offering tax incentives to investors.
